method.pairing: Adjacent AB/BA runs (1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8); calculate final_ns / baseline_ns - 1 per pair, then median of four pair ratios for each benchmark. B/op and allocs/op compared as exact unique values across four samples/state.

negative_controls.all_multi_buffer_shapes: four512 and four2048 retain identical B/op and allocs/op in baseline/final for all four consumers (576/14 and 648/16 respectively).
negative_controls.full_buffer_8192: identical 392 B/op and 10 allocs/op for all four consumers.
negative_controls.interpretation: For each API's own actual threshold+1/full/multibuffer control, allocation/byte counts are unchanged; CPU medians show small local fluctuations, not a universal gain. Do not infer a generalized or WAN throughput gain.

limitations: Benchmark code is an in-process public-writer harness, not production traffic; no singleton prevalence, WAN, server, or full-core throughput claim.
The recomputation parses raw stdout recorded by optimizer and independently pairs/aggregates the eight samples; no benchmark was rerun by verifier.
Separate summary medians are not substituted for paired-ratio calculation.
